newsitem.title: JAPAN: ISUZU MOTORS SEES LOWER 1997/98 THAI OUTPUT.
newsitem.headline: ISUZU MOTORS SEES LOWER 1997/98 THAI OUTPUT.

text.p: Isuzu Motors Ltd said on Thursday it expects its Thai vehicle output to fall in fiscal year 1997/98, ending in March, from the previous business year.

"Output (in Thailand) of our large- and medium-sized trucks is expected to drop by more than 30 percent this business year, but we have not decided yet how much we will reduce output of our mainline pick-up trucks," an Isuzu spokesman said.
The Japanese car maker said it produced 100,000 pick-up trucks and 19,000 medium- and large-sized trucks in Thailand in 1996/97.
"Factors such as the devaluation of the (Thai) baht and a rise in interest rates (in Thailand) are affecting our business there," the spokesman said.
"We will lower production in the short term, but we are still examining the situation on a long-term basis," he said.
